text.heading: Gene set benchmark dose analysis
paragraphs: Hepatic gene expression profiling in female Sprague Dawley rats exposed to 1,2-Dichlorobenzene (1,2-DCB) identified 1,062 dose-responsive genes, of which 799 (75%) were upregulated and 263 (25%) were downregulated, with benchmark doses (BMDs) spanning 12.5 to 1,020 ppm. The predominance of upregulated transcripts indicates a broadly activating hepatic stress response rather than a generalized suppression of liver function. The most significantly enriched pathways (FDR < 1 × 10⁻¹⁰) were cancer-associated signaling networks (hsa05200/rno05200) driven by a 14-gene set including NFE2L2, KEAP1, HMOX1, NQO1, HIF1A, TP53, MDM2, BAX, BAK1, CASP3, NFKB1, MAPK1, HSP90AA1, and FGF21, reflecting convergent activation of oxidative stress, DNA damage, and cell survival signaling rather than neoplastic transformation per se. Fluid thiols-based sensing through the KEAP1-NRF2 axis was a dominant mechanistic theme, with the Fluid thiols-based sensing through the KEAP1-NRF2 axis represented across multiple enriched terms including fluid thiols-based sensing through the KEAP1-NRF2 axis (hsa05418, FDR = 6.6 × 10⁻⁷), chemical carcinogenesis-reactive oxygen species (hsa05208, FDR = 4.4 × 10⁻⁶), and ferroptosis (hsa04216, FDR = 5.8 × 10⁻⁶). The ferroptosis pathway was represented by a complete five-gene set (GCLC, GCLM, GPX4, HMOX1, TP53), all upregulated, consistent with an adaptive cytoprotective response to lipid peroxidation stress [P8]. Gene Ontology enrichment corroborated these findings: \"response to xenobiotic stimulus\" (GO:0009410, FDR = 1.5 × 10⁻³⁶, 104 genes) and \"xenobiotic metabolic process\" (GO:0006805, FDR = 4.7 × 10⁻¹⁴, 35 genes) were the most broadly represented biological process terms, encompassing phase I enzymes (CYP2E1, CYP1A2, CYP2B1), phase II conjugating enzymes (GSTA2, GSTA3, GSTM2, GSTP1, UGT1A1, UGT2B7), and efflux transporters (ABCC1, ABCC2, ABCB11), indicating a coordinated xenobiotic biotransformation response. Lipid metabolic process (GO:0006629, FDR = 9.5 × 10⁻¹⁹, 103 genes) and fatty acid metabolic process (GO:0006631, FDR = 2.9 × 10⁻¹¹, 40 genes) were also highly enriched, with the majority of constituent genes upregulated, consistent with peroxisomal and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation induction (ACOX1, ACOX2, ACADM, HADH, HADHB, ECH1, ECI1) alongside lipogenic signals (FASN, SCD1, ELOVL5). Apoptotic signaling was represented bidirectionally: both \"negative regulation of apoptotic process\" (GO:0043066, 87 genes) and \"positive regulation of apoptotic process\" (GO:0043065, 54 genes) were significantly enriched, reflecting concurrent pro-survival (MCL1, BIRC5, BCL2L1, MDM2) and pro-apoptotic (BAX, BAK1, CASP3, BID, BNIP3) transcriptional changes that together suggest a cellular stress state poised between adaptation and injury [P1].

text.heading: Gene benchmark dose analysis
paragraphs: Among the 1,062 dose-responsive genes, the most literature-supported and biologically central were NFE2L2, KEAP1, HMOX1, NQO1, GCLC, and GCLM, which collectively define the canonical NRF2 antioxidant response. These genes were upregulated across a BMD range of approximately 134–241 ppm and are well-established transcriptional targets of KEAP1-NRF2 signaling activated by electrophilic and oxidative insults [P8]. GCLC, GCLM, HMOX1, NQO1, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 have been validated as robust NRF2 activity biomarkers across multiple cell types and species [P8, P11], lending high confidence to the interpretation that 1,2-DCB activates hepatic NRF2 signaling in a dose-dependent manner. CYP2E1, which was among the responsive genes in the metabolic pathway cluster (hsa01100, median BMD ~162 ppm), is of particular mechanistic relevance given its established role in the oxidative bioactivation of chlorobenzenes to reactive quinone and epoxide intermediates that can deplete glutathione and generate reactive oxygen species. The upregulation of CYP2E1 alongside GCLC, GCLM, and NQO1 is consistent with a feed-forward oxidative stress mechanism in which bioactivation-derived electrophiles trigger NRF2-mediated cytoprotective gene expression [P21]. GPX4, a phospholipid hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase critical for suppressing ferroptosis, was upregulated with a BMD within the ferroptosis pathway cluster (median ~165 ppm), and its co-induction with GCLC, GCLM, and HMOX1 suggests that lipid peroxidation is an early hepatic stress signal following 1,2-DCB exposure [P8]. TP53, MDM2, BAX, BAK1, and CASP3 were upregulated with BMDs in the range of approximately 149–244 ppm, consistent with DNA damage checkpoint activation and apoptotic priming. The concurrent upregulation of MDM2 alongside TP53 is consistent with a negative feedback loop that may limit the extent of apoptotic commitment at intermediate doses.
